claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions. Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children would you like to claim Child Benefit for?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I have one child - my son Alex. He's 8 years old and I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have one child, Alex, who is 8 years old.

To assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to ask you a few more questions:

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to understand your relationship with Alex:

**Does Alex live with you, or if he doesn't live with you, do you contribute at least the same amount as Child Benefit would be (or equivalent support) towards his care - such as for food, clothes, or pocket money?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives with me at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Just a couple more questions to complete the assessment:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! One final question:

**Is Alex currently in hospital, care, or residential accommodation, or has he been for an extended period?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, he was in care for a little while actually - it was about 8 weeks.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for sharing that. I need a bit more detail to assess this properly:

**Is Alex currently still in care, or has he returned home? And if he's returned home, when did he come back?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's back home with me now. That period in care has ended.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. Just to make sure I have all the details:

**During those 8 weeks when Alex was in care, did he spend at least 24 hours a week at home with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he was in care full-time during those 8 weeks. He didn't come home during that period.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. Let me assess Alex's eligibility for Child Benefit based on what you've told me.

Based on the rules:
- Alex is 8 years old (under 16) ✓
- You live in the UK ✓
- Alex lives with you now ✓
- No one else is claiming Child Benefit for him ✓
- Alex was in care for 8 weeks full-time, but he is now back home with you ✓

According to the rules, Child Benefit payments are affected if a child goes into care for **more than 8 weeks**. Since Alex was in care for exactly 8 weeks (not more than 8 weeks) and is now back home living with you, you should be eligible to claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.text:
**Good news! You are ELIGIBLE to claim Child Benefit for Alex.**

You meet all the requirements:
- Alex is under 16 years old
- You live in the UK
- Alex lives with you
- No one else is claiming Child Benefit for him
- His 8-week period in care does not disqualify you, as the rules only affect payments if a child is in care for **more than** 8 weeks

If you haven't already claimed, you can apply for Child Benefit. If you have any other questions about the application process, please let me know!
